headline: Highest risk is medium: Goose can write/modify shared files and use MCP, while LightZero is non-writing and non-networked, so prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict are limited but not impossible via shared filesystem workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, and its shared-state model is via filesystem, so it can ingest attacker-controlled files. LightZero is non-interactive and has no I/O surfaces, so it is not a source of injection, but it can still be the target if Goose writes prompts into shared files. The pathway exists in default file-based workflows.
conditions: IF Goose reads instructions from files in a shared cwd
IF LightZero outputs are copied into files that Goose later parses as prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable file-based prompt ingestion in Goose
Require explicit human review before Goose acts on file contents
Use read-only mounts for LightZero artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, and can egress broadly to configured model providers and MCP servers, so sensitive file contents can leave the machine. LightZero itself has no filesystem or network access, but if both share a workspace, Goose can exfiltrate data that LightZero merely co-locates. This is a default-config risk for Goose, not for LightZero.
conditions: IF Goose is pointed at a workspace containing secrets or proprietary code
IF Goose is configured with external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Run Goose in a scrubbed workspace
Remove secrets from shared directories
Restrict Goose egress to approved endpoints
Use separate OS users for the two agents
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound model traffic

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem and modify git state, while LightZero cannot write, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main risk is Goose overwriting files LightZero reads. Because only one side has mutable capabilities, the conflict blast radius is small and not symmetric.
conditions: IF Goose and LightZero are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Goose modifies files that LightZero expects to remain stable
mitigations: Use separate output directories
Make LightZero inputs read-only
Serialize writes through a single owner
Commit or snapshot shared files before Goose edits them

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can produce file edits and other outputs, but LightZero has no documented action-taking or parsing surface here, so there is no strong evidence that LightZero will treat Goose's output as authoritative. The pairwise cascade is therefore limited to manual handoff workflows, which are lower risk than default automated chaining.
conditions: IF a human copies Goose output into LightZero inputs
IF an external orchestrator feeds Goose-generated text into LightZero without verification
mitigations: Add a human verification step
Use structured, typed handoff files
Reject free-form text as control input
Log and diff Goose outputs before reuse

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles source code and files in cwd and may send them to external model providers, which can create policy issues if those files contain regulated data. LightZero has no declared data classes or network egress, so it does not add a separate compliance burden. The mismatch is mainly about Goose's outbound processing of local data, not a pairwise residency conflict.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains regulated data
IF Goose is configured to send that data to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose workspaces
Use an approved local model backend
Redact sensitive files before processing
Document retention and deletion rules
requires-engineering: add residency controls to outbound providers
